records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items`, a property that exists in no browser's flexbox implementation, so the IE10 path this mixin family targets silently gets no cross-axis alignment. IE10 users get top-aligned header contents and small-action rows while every other browser gets centered ones — a layout that differs by browser and an impossible-to-debug dead declaration for the next maintainer.
records.rationale: The diff’s `@mixin align-items($alignment)` does emit a bogus `-ms-align-items`, but it also emits the correct IE10 flexbox property `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` (see `@mixin align-items` in `mixins.scss`). That contradicts the finding’s core claim that “the IE10 path … gets no cross-axis alignment” and that IE10 users will be top-aligned; IE10 can use `-ms-flex-align` for cross-axis alignment, so alignment is not silently absent per the diff.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The flexbox mixins mix three incompatible spec generations in one declaration set (2009 `-moz-box`/`-webkit-box`, 2012 draft `-ms-flexbox`, and final `flex`), so browsers on the 2009 spec parse the box display value but then evaluate `order`/`align-items` under old-spec semantics (e.g. `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, `-webkit-box-align` keyword sets differ). Legacy Android/iOS WebKit browsers render the header with the old box model's sizing/ordering rules while modern browsers use final flexbox, producing two divergent layouts from one mixin; the old-spec declarations also cannot be removed piecemeal later without re-editing every call site.
records.rationale: The diff adds new flexbox-related mixins in `mixins.scss` that explicitly combine multiple flexbox spec generations in one ruleset: `@mixin flexbox()` sets `display: -webkit-box; -moz-box; -ms-flexbox; -webkit-flex; flex;`, while `@mixin align-items($alignment)` and `@mixin order($val)` emit both 2009 box properties (`-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) and modern flex properties (`align-items`, `order`). records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `.panel` gets `@include order(3)` and `.extra-info-wrapper` gets `order(2)`, but every other direct child of the now-flex `.contents` (`.title` at default order 0, plus any plugin/banner-injected children) is unordered, so any element appended to `.contents` by a plugin lands visually before the title rather than in DOM order. Plugin authors and future theme components that insert elements into `.d-header .contents` get their elements reordered to the far left of the header with no way to know they must now also set an `order` value — the layout contract of the header's child list changed silently.
records.rationale: The diff makes `.d-header .contents` a flex container (`@include flexbox();`) and assigns explicit ordering to at least one known child: `.panel { ... @include order(3); }` (header.scss). In flexbox, any new/unaware direct child of `.contents` will default to `order: 0` and therefore render before the explicitly ordered items (e.g., before the `.panel` with order 3), which is a real layout-contract change that could affect plugin/theme-injected header children. The finding’s mention of `.extra-info-wrapper` is less directly supported for the header (it’s changed in topic.scss, not header.scss)

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `.valign-helper` float/clear-based vertical centering scaffold is left in place inside the same `.contents` that the diff converts to flexbox, leaving two competing layout mechanisms on one container. The next developer editing the header must reason about a float-based helper whose behavior inside a flex container is undefined-ish (it becomes a flex item rather than a float helper), and cannot tell whether removing it is safe — change-risk for every future header tweak.
records.rationale: In `header.scss`, the diff converts `.contents` from a float-based layout to flex (`@include flexbox();` + `@include align-items(center);`) and removes the `.title { float: left; }` / `.panel { float: right; }` rules, but it leaves the `.valign-helper` scaffold in the same header stylesheet immediately after `.contents` (no changes/removal shown). Given `.contents` is now a flex container, any legacy float/clear-based “valign helper” used within that header layout risks becoming redundant/confusing for future edits (mixed layout mechanisms), even if it may still work.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `.small-action-desc` drops the `4em` left padding that aligned the description text under the avatar column and replaces it with `0 1.5%` percent padding, removing the avatar/text alignment with no flex sizing (`flex`, `margin`, or `gap`) on `.topic-avatar` to replace it. Users with custom avatars or wider category badges see the small-action description text start immediately adjacent to the avatar edge rather than indented beneath it, and `1.5%` padding computes against the container width so the gap varies with viewport while the avatar width is fixed — the alignment drifts at every screen size.
records.rationale: In `topic-post.scss`, `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em;` (explicit left indent likely matching the avatar column) to `padding: 0 1.5%;` while `.small-action` becomes a flex container via `@include flexbox()`/`@include align-items(center)`. The diff does not add any compensating flex sizing/spacing (`flex`, `gap`, fixed width, or margins) on `.topic-avatar` or between the avatar and description, so the previous fixed alignment/indent is removed and replaced with viewport-dependent percent padding, matching the finding’s described mechanism.
